_: The Pixie Dust Industries brand tokens. This file is the source; site/app/brand.css is generated from it by build.mjs, and never edited by hand. The direction is Risograph: three ink drums plus a black drum, printed on uncoated stock. Its whole argument is physical constraint — a fixed number of drums, translucent ink, paper showing through, registration that never quite lands — because constraints are the thing a generator cannot fake. Every contrast figure here was computed, not estimated.

house.name: Pixie Dust Industries
house._: The house is Pixie Dust Industries. The thing it ships is the Product OS. The package id stays oolio-pm and the repository stays niel-cody/oolio-product-os: those are addresses, not the brand, and every installed reference depends on them.

press._: A Riso runs one ink per pass and the drum is reloaded between them. Three is the practical ceiling before the paper starts to buckle, so three is the palette — not a restriction to work around, the reason the look holds together.

stock._: Uncoated cool grey. Riso ink is translucent, so it needs a pale sheet to sit on; the process physically cannot print on dark stock. This is why the site is light.

stock-2.use: a second sheet, lifted: cards, plates, panels

stock-3.use: recessed, a gutter or a well

rule.use: a hairline division inside a plate. Never a keyline

drums._: One drum per pass, in order. The number is the pass.

pink.use: The dust. Out of gamut, unmixable in CMYK, and the ink people recognise as Riso on sight. The moment that matters on a page, never a whole surface. A fill, a rule, a ghost layer, or a button ground carrying black type.

blue.use: The industry. A dusty federal navy that carries structure, rules and diagrams. The only drum besides black that may set copy.

yellow.use: The spark. Third drum, smallest budget, reserved for the human sign-off gates. As the only warm thing on the sheet, 'a person decides here' becomes the loudest mark on the map.

k.use: Never #000. A Riso black lays down a soft warm neutral that sits on the paper rather than punching a hole in it. All body copy runs here, and so does every keyline.

overprints._: Translucent ink multiplies where two passes cross. These are not chosen; the press produces them. That is why they are worth more than a fourth drum.

type-colour._: What words are set in. Body copy is the black drum; everything here is a step of it, and each figure is measured on the stock.

soft-ink.use: a secondary paragraph, or long copy that should sit back

muted-ink.use: captions, eyebrows and the mono furniture. The last step that clears AA

faint-ink.use: decoration only. Never a word a person has to read

semantic._: The lifecycle map's six meanings, drawn from the ink set rather than a colour wheel. Seven inks exist once the overprints are counted, and there are seven things to say, so nothing had to be invented.

gate.means: a person decides here. The third drum, and the whole argument

orch.means: orchestration: a skill driving a tool. Blue carries structure

loop.means: learning returning upstream. The reason this is a system and not a pipeline, so it gets the signature ink

signal.means: raw input, before anyone has shaped it. Uncoloured on purpose: colouring it would be a claim about it

moves._: Riso on the web is four techniques. Get these right and everything else is ordinary layout; get them wrong and it is a filter over a SaaS site.

grain.how: fractalNoise at baseFrequency 0.82, four octaves, multiplied over the page in one position:fixed pass
grain.why: Fixed, so it never scrolls with the content: the sheet stays still while the ink moves. Around 18 to 20 per cent is the line between paper and dirty screen.

overprint.how: mix-blend-mode: multiply on the ink layer, isolation: isolate on its parent
overprint.why: Ink is translucent, so shapes darken where they cross instead of hiding each other. Without the isolation the blend escapes its container.

halftone.how: radial-gradient dots, one screen angle per drum
halftone.why: A Riso cannot do continuous tone; it screens everything into dots. Two drums at the same angle produce moiré, which is why the angles are fixed.

misregistration.how: two ghost copies behind the solid, both multiplying
misregistration.budget: once per screen, display type only
misregistration.why: The paper shifts between passes so the plates never quite line up. It is a signature, not a texture: overdone it stops reading as a press and starts reading as a filter.

display.use: the wordmark and headlines. Drawn for a French art centre, not a startup: wide, slightly wrong proportions, and it reads as an art press rather than a design system

text.use: everything a person reads. A grotesque built for small sizes and dense text, doing nothing interesting on purpose so Syne can

system.use: every label, ink code, screen angle, count, stamp and slash command. Typewriter rather than terminal

shape._: Print has keylines, not rounded cards. A radius anywhere on this brand is a mistake unless a real component needs it.

out.use: a plate settling: entering and exiting

motion._noEaseIn: There is deliberately no ease-in. It delays the moment being watched most, which is what makes an interface feel sluggish at an identical duration.

mark._: The Gate, carried over and re-inked. The ring is the loop, the break is where it does not close on its own, and the bead is the person who closes it. The bead is Sun Yellow because Sun Yellow is the human-gate drum, so the meaning survives the change of palette intact.
mark.clearSpace: one bead diameter (6 units on the 32 grid) on every side

aliases._: The names the site already speaks, kept pointing at the right ink so no component had to be rewritten to be reprinted.
